claim: For fixed m, the number of solutions of m/n = 1/a1+1/a2+1/a3 is at most O_eps(n^{3/5+eps}), improving a 2011 result of Browning and Elsholtz and extending Elsholtz-Tao (2013), who proved this only for m=4 with n prime.
stance_target: upper bound on multiplicity of a single three-term unit-fraction representation
scope_conditions: general fixed numerator m, general n (not restricted to primes)
quoted_support: In particular, for fixed m there are at most O_eps(n^{3/5+eps}) solutions of m/n=1/a1+1/a2+1/a3. This improves upon a result of Browning and Elsholtz (2011) and extends a result of Elsholtz and Tao (2013) who proved this when m=4 and n is a prime.

claim: For given m, in every reduced residue class e mod f, infinitely many primes p have >> exp((5 log 2/(12 lcm(m,f)) + o(1)) log p / log log p) solutions to m/p = 1/a1+1/a2+1/a3, improving the prior lower bound of order (log p)^0.549.
stance_target: lower bound on multiplicity of a single three-term unit-fraction representation
scope_conditions: fixed numerator m, primes p in a residue class mod f
quoted_support: we prove that for given m in N in every reduced residue class e mod f there exist infinitely many primes p such that the number of solutions of the equation m/p=1/a1+1/a2+1/a3 is >>_{f,m} exp((5 log 2/(12 lcm(m,f))+o_{f,m}(1)) log p/log log p). Previously the best known lower bound of this type was of order (log p)^0.549.

claim: An algorithm exists finding all solutions of m/n=1/a1+1/a2+1/a3 in expected running time O_eps(n^eps (n^3/m^2)^{1/5}).
stance_target: computational tractability of enumerating three-term unit fraction representations
quoted_support: there exists an algorithm finding all solutions in expected running time O_eps(n^eps(n^3/m^2)^{1/5}), for any eps>0.
